title: Christ makes bad trees good
source_text: II. Verum eos qui per naturam arbores putres & malae sunt Christus gratiae suae efficacia bonas arbores reddit. Homines enim per Spiritum suum, a corruptione peccati repurgat atque sanctificat, efficitque ut veterem hominem exuentes, novum hominem induant, & fiant novae creaturae, neque amplius peccato, sed justitiae serviant.
pass_a_gloss: II. But those who by nature are rotten & bad trees Christ by the efficacy of his grace renders good trees. For by his Spirit he cleanses men from the corruption of sin & sanctifies them, & brings it about that, putting off the old man, they put on the new man, & become new creatures, & no longer serve sin, but righteousness.
pass_b_english: Thesis II. Christ, by the power of his grace, makes good trees out of those who are rotten and bad by nature. Through his Spirit he cleanses people from the corruption of sin and makes them holy.
He causes them to strip off the old self and put on the new, to become new creations, and to serve righteousness rather than sin from now on.

lemmas.gloss: by the efficacy of his grace

lemmas.latin: veterem hominem exuentes, novum hominem induant
lemmas.gloss: putting off the old man, they put on the new man

choices.why: Christ's image of the good and the bad tree (Matt. 7:17-18), which frames the whole locus: the person must be made good before the works can be.
